body:
Nick Halloway (snowe@rain.org) wrote:
: Which says that the definition of what is "crazy" is not the 
: particular actions or beliefs, it's whether they have the 
: support of a substantial number of other people.  "Crazy" means
: not fitting in, means alienation from *one's immediate society*.
: Being alienated from humans in other countries is not 
: considered crazy.  "Crazy" has an interpersonal definition.  If
: the person to be judged on "craziness" is a working part of
: some immediate society which has the approval of the person
: judging them, they will not be called "crazy", not matter how
: violent their actions or their emotions or how many visions they see.

Yep, it's herd morality at its worst.

155.  Our society tends to regard as a "sickness" any mode of thought
      or behavior that is inconvenient for the system, and this is
      plausible because when an individual doesn't fit into the system
      it causes pain to the individual as well as problems for the system.
      Thus the manipulation of an individual to adjust him to the system
      is seen as a "cure" for a "sickness" and therefore as good.

-Ric
